svg.aria-label: How much of the load a read cache can absorb as the write share of traffic rises. The left column is the measured case from this experiment, at roughly eight per cent writes, where a cache can absorb almost all of the read traffic. The two columns to its right are reasoning rather than measurement, marked as such: at twenty per cent writes and at fifty per cent writes, less and less of the load can be served from a cache. Two reasons are given: a write can never be served from a cache, and a write invalidates the entry that other readers were about to use. The caption says to measure the read to write mix before choosing caching as the fix, because the mix rather than the traffic volume decides whether it is the right lever at all.
svg.text: A READ CACHE IS ONLY AS GOOD AS THE READ SHARE

text.font-family: ui-sans-serif, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
